module purpose: neorv32_pwm decodes bus accesses into per-channel PWM configuration words, returns selected channel configuration on the bus, OR-reduces channel enable requests into clkgen_en_o, and maps channel PWM bits into pwm_o. Each neorv32_pwm_channel stores enable, prescaler, polarity, divider, and duty settings, then uses clkgen_i, local counters, and clk_i to generate its PWM output.

use-case flows.value: selected channel configuration word written from bus data into the channel enable, prescaler, polarity, divider, and duty registers
selected channel configuration word returned from the channel registers through rdata_o, OR-reduced into rdata_sum, and placed into the bus response with acknowledge
per-channel enable state copied to the channel clock-generator request and OR-reduced to the top-level clkgen_en_o
selected clkgen_i source and divider generate cnt_tick, the duty counter advances, and pwm_o is driven from cfg_pol and the cnt_duty-versus-cfg_duty comparison
bus response forced to rsp_terminate_c and channel configuration, counters, and PWM outputs cleared while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel read and write strobe decisions
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure and read-out flows depend on the final per-channel strobes computed from address, strobe, and access type: `sel(i) <= ...` (line 109), `we(i) <= sel(i) and bus_req_i.stb and (bus_req_i.rw);` (line 110), and `re(i) <= sel(i) and bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw);` (line 111). The channel consumes these decisions in `if (we_i = '1') then` to update configuration (lines 183-188) and in the qualified readback assignment at line 194. Integrity matters because wrong strobes write or read the wrong channel; availability is conditional on the matching address, stb, and rw conditions being present.

The channel stores an enable bit from `wdata_i(31)` at line 184 when `we_i = '1'` (line 183). This stored setting gates the divider and duty counters at lines 212 and 224 and participates in the PWM output decision at line 231, so corrupting it changes whether the channel counts or idles. Availability is also established because the setting is held in cfg_en, returned on readback at line 194, and exported as the channel clock-generator enable request at line 197.

The channel stores `cfg_prsc <= wdata_i(30 downto 28);` at line 185 when `we_i = '1'`. This setting selects which `clkgen_i` bit is tested in `clkgen_i(to_integer(unsigned(cfg_prsc))) = '1'` at line 214, so its integrity determines the clock source used for PWM timing. Availability is established because the setting is held in cfg_prsc and returned on readback at line 194.

The channel stores `cfg_cdiv <= wdata_i(17 downto 8);` at line 187 when `we_i = '1'`. The divider counter compares against this stored value at line 215, resets at line 216, and asserts cnt_tick at line 217, so integrity of cfg_cdiv is required for correct PWM timing. Availability is established because the setting is held in cfg_cdiv and returned on readback at line 194.

The channel stores `cfg_duty <= wdata_i(7 downto 0);` at line 188 when `we_i = '1'`. The PWM output decision compares `unsigned(cnt_duty) >= unsigned(cfg_duty)` at line 231 and then drives pwm_o at lines 232 and 234, so integrity of cfg_duty is required for correct pulse width. Availability is established because the setting is held in cfg_duty and returned on readback at line 194.

The channel stores `cfg_pol <= wdata_i(27);` at line 186 when `we_i = '1'`. The PWM output then drives `cfg_pol` at line 232 and `not cfg_pol` at line 234, so integrity of cfg_pol is required for correct active/inactive output polarity. Availability is established because the setting is held in cfg_pol and returned on readback at line 194.

The operate flow depends on the live sequencing state held in cnt_cdiv, cnt_tick, and cnt_duty. When enabled, the selected `clkgen_i` source drives cnt_cdiv until `cnt_cdiv = cfg_cdiv` (lines 214-219), cnt_tick is raised on that terminal count (line 217), and cnt_duty advances on cnt_tick (lines 226-227). The current cnt_duty state is then consumed by the PWM output comparison at line 231. Integrity of this state matters because wrong counts or tick events change waveform timing; availability is conditional on `cfg_en = '1'` and matching clkgen_i pulses. The flow graph lists cnt_tick as constant-valued because its assigned values are literals, but RTL lines 211-217 show it is a computed event controlled by cfg_en, cfg_prsc, cfg_cdiv, cnt_cdiv, and clkgen_i.

The channel computes its PWM output from the enable state and the duty comparison at line 231, then drives `pwm_o <= cfg_pol;` at line 232 or `pwm_o <= not cfg_pol;` at line 234. The top entity places the instantiated channel outputs onto the external vector in `pwm_o(pwm'range) <= pwm(pwm'range);` (line 117) after clearing the full vector at line 116. Integrity requires the delivered output level to match the current settings and counters; availability is established by reset to `'0'` at line 207 and clocked updates on each rising edge thereafter.

Each channel exports `clkgen_en_o <= cfg_en;` at line 197, these per-channel requests are connected to ce at line 104, and the top entity drives `clkgen_en_o <= or_reduce_f(ce);` at line 121. This establishes a computed decision that an external clock-generation consumer depends on: whether any channel is enabled. Integrity requires the exported request to equal the OR of the channel enable states; availability holds whenever at least one enabled channel exists.
